summary: Two small range lights on the Outer Wharf at Cape Tormentine, New Brunswick, set up for the steamer Stanley's winter runs to Prince Edward Island in the early 1900s.

structures.note: 32-foot tower with a fourth-order lens (LighthouseFriends, 1908); a fixed red catoptric light on a freight-shed window from 1902. The present front light is a pepperpot tower put in place in the 1940s (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett gives 11 m / 33 ft).
Rowlett gives 12.5 m (40 ft); LighthouseFriends gives 32 ft to the ventilator. The 1902 rear light was shown from an iceboat-house cupola.

access.note: Owned by the Canadian Coast Guard. LighthouseFriends: grounds and tower closed; a fence across the last part of the wharf. Rowlett: site open, tower closed; a company fenced the wharf in 2004, and access is reported restored since.

notes_for_editor: 1) First light: Rowlett and the record say 1901 (cite 1); LighthouseFriends says Artemis Lord set them up in 1902 (cite 2); the 1902 report says they 'have been established' and credits Mr. Lord with the aids (cite 3). Not resolved; the story gives both. 2) Status: the Coast Guard list gives the front light as Iso R 2s, Seasonal (cite 6); LighthouseFriends says it was reactivated in 1998 and is maintained by the Coast Guard (cite 2); Rowlett says inactive since 2022, after Hurricane Fiona (cite 1). Not resolved; the record's own conflict list records the same disagreement. 3) Rear tower height: LighthouseFriends gives 32 ft to the ventilator (cite 2); Rowlett gives 12.5 m (40 ft) (cite 1). The story does not give a rear height. 4) Keepers: all four keeper stints come from LighthouseFriends (cite 2). Barry's 1907 entry (cite 5) was matched by row position and checked on the page image (scan 149): the appointment column reads 26 Mar. 1906. Wall, Allen and C. T. Wall are not corroborated by any source read. 5) Not used: the Department's keeper table for the year ended 30 June 1900 lists E. T. Allen at Cape Tormentine from 20 October 1897, which belongs to the separate Cape Tormentine lighthouse. 6) Distances in the 1902 and 1903 reports are printed as miles and are not converted to nautical miles. 7) The 1903 report's pier statement (cite 4) is in the 'Report of the Deputy Minister' (signed F. Gourdeau), a report on a trip of inspection with the Minister, not an inspector's report. 8) The 1908 report (not cited) describes a new rear tower 70 feet back from the iceboat house and the cupola light discontinued; not used. 9) Not found: any Department record of the rear tower's ownership transfer, and any source for keepers' duties. Wikipedia was not used. 10) The 1917 Entrance range lights and the Indian Point range (Rowlett) are separate stations and are not covered here.
